description: ago(ts, now) — the pt-PT relative-time string shown under a report. Uses Math.round, floored to a minimum of 1 so nothing ever reads 'há 0 min'. Two boundary cases below ('há 60 min' and 'há 24 h') look like off-by-one bugs but are the real, current output of domain.js — rounding pushes the display over the branch's own cutoff. They are included deliberately so a port that 'fixes' the rounding gets caught by this vector; if domain.js is ever intentionally changed here, update these cases in the same commit.

cases.description: Report filed at the same instant as now: floored to 'há 1 min', never 'há 0 min'.
10s rounds to 0 min unfloored; the Math.max(1, …) floor kicks in.
90s / 60s = 1.5, rounds up to 2 — no flooring needed here.
3599999ms is still under hourMs so it takes the minutes branch; 3599999/60000 = 59.99998, which rounds to 60. Reads 'há 60 min', not 'há 1 h' — the known rounding quirk.
At exactly hourMs the diff no longer qualifies for the minutes branch (d < hourMs is false), so it takes the hours branch: 1 h.
86399999ms is still under dayMs so it takes the hours branch; 86399999/3600000 rounds to 24. Reads 'há 24 h', not 'há 1 d' — the same rounding quirk as the 60-min case.
At exactly dayMs the diff no longer qualifies for the hours branch, so it takes the days branch: 1 d.
There is no upper branch — the days branch is used forever, however old the report.
